input.quote: Vendor grants Customer alone a non-transferable licence, revocable at Vendor's sole discretion, to use the Services without Affiliates or contractors.
input.rationale: Section 13.1 grants the subscription licence to Customer only, expressly excludes Affiliates and contractors, is non-transferable, and is revocable at Vendor's sole discretion — the playbook walk-away position. It also conflicts with Section 13.2 (paid-up licence to Customer and Affiliates with contractor support), Section 13.3 (transfer to Affiliate/successor; no revocation except for uncured breach after notice), and Section 24.1 (assignment to Affiliates/successors). The redline extends the licence to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, removes discretionary revocation by tying suspension/revocation to Section 13.3, and confirms transferability, reaching the preferred position with a minimal edit.

proposal.summary: Extend the subscription licence in 13.1 to Affiliates and contractors, remove revocation at Vendor's discretion, and confirm transferability
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have extended the subscription licence to our Affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf, removed Vendor's right to revoke at its sole discretion, and confirmed transferability to an Affiliate or successor, so that Section 13.1 aligns with Sections 13.2, 13.3, and 24. Our position is that a licence must not be revocable at will; if helpful, we can cover Affiliates on written notice as a fallback.

ops.oldText: Vendor grants Customer alone a non-transferable licence, revocable at Vendor's sole discretion, to use the Services without Affiliates or contractors.
ops.newText: Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates, and contractors acting on Customer's or an Affiliate's behalf, a non-exclusive, worldwide licence to access and use the Services during the applicable subscription term. Customer may transfer that licence as permitted by Section 13.3 and Section 24, and Vendor may revoke or suspend it only as permitted by Section 13.3.
